design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DESIGN DOSSIER — employer_charge_protests task 0 (category charge).

[0] Draw and claim. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. The tree has exactly one prerequisite problem; charge_ext_protest_amount (the employer's protest, user write) takes 6 factors and charge_ext_protest_relief_credit (the protest decision, agent write, root) takes 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: the protest event (charge_protest_filed, user tool file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2) and the protest-granted event (charge_protest_granted, agent tool grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5, 4]): the notice-of-claim answer (charge_separation_response_filed, user) and the relief determination on it (charge_relief_determined, agent) — an independent two-problem tree on a different base policy pair (charge_evt_notice_and_response, charge_evt_relief_grounds as determination), so the headroom check holds.

[1] Why this is a good test. The caller (practice administrator of Saint Odile Community Clinic, a reimbursing nonprofit) only asks to have the third-quarter 2026 charges for a former aide removed because the clinic's 2025 wages for her were reported twice. Nothing in the request names a protest. The agent must read in the protest-decision rule that "The relief credit of a protest decision is fixed only after the position carries a pending written protest of the statement, with the protest ground and the protest date recorded on it", see on the position that status is chargeable and protest ground none, work out from the protest-amount rule that the write which records a protest is the employer's own written protest, compute the amount protested (six factors over the statement, the clinic's reimbursement bill, credits posted outside the statement's quarter, amended wage reports, the unanswered notice and bill interest), hand the protest to the caller, and only then compute the relief credit (four factors) on the world in which the protest exists, booking it against the one charge that still stands. Difficulty comes from reading rules and reconciling records (12 charges, 11 credits of two reasons in two quarters, a statement, a bill, interest, a payment, 12 wage reports), not from choosing between similar tools.

[2] Problem-tree card. Root: charge_ext_protest_relief_credit. Edge root -> charge_ext_protest_amount: kind value_input, gate protest_ground_recorded (compute binding F('protest_ground')), form state, policy_source (prerequisite sentence, affirmative direction, in the root's own rule) "The relief credit of a protest decision is fixed only after the position carries a pending written protest of the statement, with the protest ground and the protest date recorded on it." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after" joining the root's result (the relief credit) to what it waits on; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state of the position (a written protest carried by it, protest ground and protest date recorded) — no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id; (4) strength "only after", scope one written protest on the position. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2 sets status protest_pending, protest_date and protest_ground and records a charge_protest submission; no other tool writes protest fields. Derivation: sentence + records (position chargeable, protest ground none, protest date empty, no charge_requests row) + the protest-amount rule ("A written protest that disputes the employer's base-period wages ... states an amount protested") -> the resolving action is the employer's written protest, owner user. Condition: position in protest_pending with protest_date and protest_ground other than none, and a charge_protest submission on record. Seed evidence it is false at frozen_time: initial_state.charge_positions.<P0>.status = chargeable, .protest_ground = none, .protest_date = ''. Topological order: protest (step 11) then decision (step 13). Single edge, no parallel prerequisites. Deletion sensitivity (check_compute value_input run): skipping the protest leaves protest ground none -> relief reach takes the no-charge tier -> relief_credit_amount 0.00 instead of 272.16. user_scenario names no protest: its only reference is the passive branch about putting "something in writing on record" after the agent explains. Tools validate nothing: both tool bodies are plain ctx.create/ctx.update calls.

[3] Base-invariant card. Write 1 (charge_protest_filed): governing base policy charge_evt_statement_and_protest, gate protest_window (time): condition "A protest is accepted only when it is received no later than the protest window after the statement mailing date."; anchor event the statement mailing date, anchor source charge_ledger.statement_mailed_date (statement row, 2026-11-12), duration variants.protest_window_days = 30, calendar days counted from the day after mailing, relation not_after, boundary inclusive -> last day 2026-12-12; frozen_time 2026-11-24 is day 12: satisfied. Just short: a protest received 2026-12-12 is timely; at/after the boundary: 2026-12-13 is not accepted. Object correlation: statement row charge_position_id = P0 and charge_quarter 2026-Q3 equal the call's charge_position_id and charge_quarter. Write 2 (charge_protest_granted): governing base policies charge_evt_relief_grounds (no structured eligibility; the reimbursing class allows wrong-wages relief: relief_not_base_period_employer true for Reimbursing Nonprofit Employer) and charge_evt_statement_and_protest (protest_window applies only to filing; scope only: decided within 30 business days — decided the same day). The protest-time status gate is respected: the position moves chargeable -> protest_pending -> relieved along the base lifecycle.

[4] Business-object card. Target object: the clinic's chargeable position P0 on claim CL0 (Marisol Fenwick-Adeyemi, Regular State UI filed 2026-06-29), statement 2026-Q3 (row stmt_q3). Charges in scope: the twelve 2026-Q3 postings (weeks ending 2026-07-11 .. 2026-09-26) totalling 4,286.10 at share 0.7000 (25,200.00 / 36,000.00). Already settled: the week ending 2026-09-26 charge (378.00) by the 2026-09-30 payment_cancelled credit (payment cancelled as issued in error on 2026-09-29); the weeks ending 2026-07-18 .. 2026-09-19 (ten charges, 3,567.90) by the 2026-10-30 overpayment_recovered credits (overpayment recovered in full). Still standing: the week ending 2026-07-11 charge, 340.20 (payment 486.00 after a 54.00 earnings deduction). The relief credit names that charge (source_charge_id post1) — the only posting with no credit against it.

[5] Factor card — charge_ext_protest_amount (6 factors, expected 274.88, all-baseline 0.00). (a) statement_starting_amount (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty taxacct): tiers reimbursing & billed -> amount billed / contributory & posted to reserve -> reserve posting / otherwise -> charges listed; evidence CFIELD taxacct variant 'Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization' and the 2026-Q3 reimbursement bill of 3,908.10; baseline (listed 4,286.10) gives 580.31. Near-miss: the listed figure 4,286.10 still includes the 378.00 cancelled charge that the bill already nets. (b) credits_taken_out (method): a recovered-overpayment credit among the credits posted in a quarter other than the statement's quarter -> every credit posted outside that quarter (3,945.90 - 378.00 = 3,567.90) / no recovery credit but cancelled-payment credits outside it -> those / otherwise nothing; baseline (nothing) gives 3,157.74; near-miss: the 2026-09-30 cancelled-payment credit sits inside 2026-Q3 and must not be taken out again (the rule says 'a quarter other than the statement's quarter', so only one reading exists). (c) protest_documentation_share (parameter, cross-difficulty taxacct): >= 4 amended reports filed within 12 months -> 1.00 / 1-3 -> 0.50 / none -> 0.00; evidence the four amended 2025 reports filed 2026-11-18; near-miss the 2024-Q4 amended report filed 2025-08-14 (15 months back); baseline 0.00 gives 0.00. (d) notice_answer_share (parameter): no separation response on record -> 0.80 / late without good cause -> 0.90 / otherwise -> 1.00; evidence: no charge_requests rows; baseline gives 343.60. (e) interest_months (method, cross-difficulty taxacct): bill paid after due -> whole months + 1 / unpaid past due -> whole months to the protest + 1 / none; bill due 2026-11-13, paid 2026-11-19 -> 1; baseline 0 gives 272.16. (f) protest_interest_basis (method, cross-difficulty taxacct): interest assessed for the quarter -> the latest assessed month in proportion to the protested principal over the billed amount / none assessed yet, reimbursing and the bill past due -> protested principal x class late-payment rate / otherwise none; the tax account shows 39.08 assessed for 2026-Q3 (accrual month 2026-11) -> 39.08 x 272.16 / 3,908.10 = 2.72153 per month; baseline (none) gives 272.16. Arithmetic: MX(0, 3,908.10 - 3,567.90) = 340.20; RND(340.20 x 1.00 x 0.80) = 272.16; RND(2.72153 x 1) = 2.72; 274.88.

[6] Factor card — charge_ext_protest_relief_credit (4 factors, expected 272.16, all-baseline 0.00). (a) relief_reach (method): wage-record ground (not_base_period_employer / wrong_wages) -> every charge posted on the claim x wage-record relief share / payment ground (agency_error / overpayment_recovered) -> charges posted in the protested quarter / otherwise -> none (baseline, the late-answer treatment of a protest given after the notice window); evidence protest ground wrong_wages recorded by step 11 and the 4,286.10 of postings; baseline 0.00. (b) credits_deducted (method): recovery credit stands -> every credit / cancelled-payment credits without recovery -> those / none -> nothing; 3,945.90 deducted; baseline gives 4,286.10 x 0.80 capped at the 340.20 still standing = 340.20. (c) wage_record_relief_share (parameter, cross-difficulty taxacct): the same amended-report count as in the protest -> 1.00; baseline 0.00 gives 0.00. (d) answer_abatement (parameter): no response on record -> 0.80; baseline 1.00 gives 340.20. RND(MX(0, 4,286.10 x 1.00 - 3,945.90) x 0.80) = 272.16.

[7] Overrides and inheritance. The relief credit replaces two base sentences, declared in overwrite: charge_evt_relief_grounds "A granted relief credits back every charge already posted within its scope" and charge_evt_credits "A relief credits the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope", both by "The relief credit of a protest decision is the relief reach, less the credits deducted from it, never below zero, times the answer abatement, rounded to the cent, and it is booked against the single posted charge that still stands within the relief reach." Everything else is inherited: once-per-reason credits and the remaining-charge cap (the credit 272.16 <= 340.20 remaining), credits on the next bill for a reimbursing employer, the protest window, protest decision days, the no-reargument rule (the wage ground was never decided). The amount protested is an extended quantity base does not define (overwrite []).

[8] initial_state rows and why. customers: the clinic (caller; phone 6085555142, FEIN last4 5142, ZIP 53781 for locate/verify) and the claimant (parent of the claim; named through find_claim_ledger customer_id). employer_accounts: the clinic's reimbursing nonprofit account (class decides the starting amount and which interest tier applies; balance 0.00 = bill 3,908.10 + interest 39.08 - payment 3,947.18). claims + claim_ledger (15 rows): entitlement, waiting week, twelve payments, the 2026-09-29 cancellation — they tie each charge to a payment and explain the cancelled-payment credit. charge_positions (1) and charge_ledger (24: 12 postings, 1 cancelled-payment credit, 10 recovery credits, 1 statement): all reconciled by both computations. employer_wage_reports (12): 2025 originals and amendments (support share evidence and near-miss), 2026 originals. employer_tax_ledger (3): bill, interest, payment (starting amount and interest months). Every row is read by a gold read (closure 59 = initial 59). Automatic clauses checked: no statement is due that is not mailed, the position is not relieved, no further charge can post (claim inactive), the cancelled payment was not reissued, so no extra obligation is lit.

[9] Persona. Delphine Marchetti-Osei, businesslike practice administrator; volunteers only the surface request and the facts the records support (third-quarter 2026 statement, duplicated 2025 wage records found by the bookkeeper, corrected reports filed November 18). Only when asked: the notice of claim in July was never answered (lost in a staff change) — matches response timeliness none; the bill was paid online on November 19 with late interest — matches the tax ledger; she knows nothing about the claimant's payments or debts. Passive reactions: agrees to lodge "something in writing" in the clinic's name with the agent's details and accepts the amount; reads back the reference if asked; closes once told the charges were decided and a credit posted, or asks once why if refused. No labels, no numbers the agent computes, no mention of a protest.

[10] Standard solution. Locate (phone) and verify (phone, FEIN last4, ZIP); read the position, its ledger, its submissions, the claim and payments, the tax account, tax ledger and wage reports; compute the amount protested (274.88) and hand file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2 to the caller with charge_quarter 2026-Q3, protest_ground wrong_wages; then compute the relief credit on the post-protest world (272.16) and call grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e with source_charge_id = the week ending 2026-07-11 charge and relief_basis not_base_period_employer (the basis covering 'the wages charged to it are wrong'). Terminal state: one protest submission, position relieved with relief basis not_base_period_employer and total charged 68.04, one new relief credit of 272.16.

[11] Places easily got wrong. Using the statement's listed 4,286.10 instead of the billed 3,908.10; taking out the in-quarter cancelled-payment credit a second time; counting the 2024-Q4 amendment; forgetting the 0.80 answer share/abatement; counting interest by whole months only (0) instead of adding the month of payment; computing the relief credit before the protest exists (0.00); booking the credit on a charge already fully credited; choosing protest ground not_base_period_employer although the clinic did employ her.

[12] Verification code and outputs. Machine face: the policies' compute blocks evaluated by skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py on the handling-time worlds (protest on initial_state; decision after replaying steps 1 and 11). Commands and outputs (final run): check_extended -> EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks -> 0.json 14 acts det True nonvac True closure 59 = init 59, REPLAY OK; check_solvability -> 0.json verify True calls 2 base gates 3 seed rows 25, SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute -> 0.json comps 2 factors 10 cross 5 history 48 branches 37, COMPUTE OK (factor sensitivities 580.31 / 3157.74 / 0.00 / 343.60 / 272.16 / 272.16 and 0.00 / 340.20 / 0.00 / 340.20 recomputed and equal to the declared figures); check_grounding -> GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire -> SCOPE OK.

[13] Solvability evidence vs GT. Step 11's protest_window evidence is the statement row's charge_position_id, charge_quarter and statement_mailed_date plus frozen_time, bound to the call's charge_position_id and charge_quarter. Step 13 rests on prior_step:11 and the position's class. Draft recomputation from the visible context only (KB rules as rendered, tool docstrings, lookup returns, persona lines): the starting amount, credits outside the statement's quarter, documentation and answer shares and one interest month give 274.88; the decision rule with the recorded wrong_wages ground gives 340.20 x 0.80 = 272.16 booked on the only uncredited charge — the same writes, order and arguments as gold.

[14] Revision log. (r1) Symptom: replay_tasks reported dangling FK employer_tax_ledger.account_request_id=''. Root cause: an empty string is treated as a foreign key value. Change: account_request_id seeded as null. Re-run: REPLAY OK. (r2) Symptom: the protest and relief policies both called their documentation measure "wage-record support share", a prose-layer collision for the KB. Change: renamed to "protest documentation share" (protest) and "wage-record relief share" (relief); factors renamed; re-run COMPUTE OK. (r3) Symptom: the relief netting tier "only credits for cancelled payments" did not match compute (which tests cancelled credits after the recovery tier). Change: tier reworded "credits for cancelled payments stand on it but none for a recovered overpayment" in rule, basis and ladder. Re-run EXTENDED OK. (r4) Schema note: charge_requests has no amount column, so the amount protested is carried by the protest submission's reference (the reference is minted from every argument) and echoed in the receipt; a wrong amount produces a different submission row and a different terminal hash. (r5, policy-audit rework round 2) F1/T0-1: credits_taken_out restated as 'credits posted in a quarter other than the statement's quarter' (rule, ladder, basis, compute names) with tier 2 'no recovery credit but cancelled-payment credits' and tier 3 'otherwise' — single reading, gold 274.88 unchanged. F4/T0-2: protest_interest_rate (with its unreal 0.005 reserve tier) removed; replaced by protest_interest_basis (method) reading the interest the tax account actually assessed on the quarter's bill — same 2.72. F2: the late-response bar is declared overwritten by the answer-abatement sentence. F3: the relief credit is capped at the charge still standing (MN), sensitivity of credits_deducted now 340.20. O3: wage-record relief share now counts reports ('number'), as computed. O4: prerequisite sentence names a pending protest. (r6, KB-audit rework round 5) P2: the monthly protest interest's first tier now also requires an amount billed for the quarter (as the compute guards the divisor). P3: interest months now count from the latest payment applied to the reimbursement bill (compute filters component reimbursement); on this world that is the same 2026-11-19 payment, so 1 month. P1/P4: the protest-decision rule now says the class term on payments before a late response is applied only through the answer abatement, and that an appeal-granted relief still credits the whole remaining charge; both are declared in the overwrites. No value moved (274.88 / 272.16).
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Marchetti-Osei, practice administrator of Saint Odile Community Clinic, a small nonprofit clinic in Fallon Springs, calling the Lakeland Department of Workforce Security on a Tuesday morning. You are businesslike and a little tired of paperwork, and you speak in full, polite sentences. The statement of benefit charges the clinic received for the third quarter of 2026 lists weekly charges for Marisol Fenwick-Adeyemi, a part-time environmental services aide the clinic laid off for lack of work in June, and you want those charges taken off the clinic's account as far as the Department's rules allow. Last week the clinic's bookkeeper found that the payroll vendor, after a system migration in January 2025, carried Marisol on two employee records for all of 2025, so every 2025 quarterly wage report the clinic filed listed her wages twice and the Department thinks the clinic paid her far more than it did. The bookkeeper filed corrected reports for all four 2025 quarters on November 18. You open by saying, in your own words, that you are calling about the charges for Marisol on the third-quarter statement, that the clinic's 2025 wages for her were reported twice by mistake, and that you want the charges removed.

When the agent asks how to find the clinic, you give the clinic's phone number, 6085555142. When asked to verify, you give the last four digits of the clinic's FEIN, 5142, and the mailing ZIP code, 53781, one at a time as the agent asks for them. You do not know any reference numbers.

You only bring up the following when the agent asks. The clinic never sent back the notice of claim for Marisol that arrived in July; you cannot find any trace of it and think it was lost during a staff change at the front desk. The clinic paid the third-quarter reimbursement bill online on November 19, a few days after it was due, and the payment included the late interest. You know nothing about Marisol's benefit payments or about anything she may owe the Department.

You want the agent to take care of the decision on the charges for the clinic. If the agent explains that the clinic itself has to put something in writing on record before the charges can be decided, you agree to do it right away; when the agent hands you the submission to lodge, you lodge it yourself in the clinic's name with exactly the details the agent reads out to you, and you accept the amount the agent gives you without arguing. If the agent asks, you read back the reference number the submission returns.

Once the agent tells you the charges have been decided and a credit has been put on the clinic's account, you thank the agent and end the call. If instead the agent says no credit can be given, you ask once why, listen to the answer, and end the call politely. You do not ask for anything else.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A protest is accepted only when it is received no later than the protest window after the statement mailing date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the statement mailing date, and a protest received on the last day is timely.

boundary_check.just_before: Counting starts the day after the 2026-11-12 mailing, so 2026-12-12 is the thirtieth and last day; a protest received on 2026-12-12 is still timely, and the protest received on 2026-11-24 (day 12) is well inside the window.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A protest received on 2026-12-13, the first day past the inclusive thirtieth day, would not be accepted and no protest could then be lodged for the 2026-Q3 statement.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_quarter: 2026-Q3. Basis: the only statement on the position is the charge_statement_issued row with charge_quarter 2026-Q3 mailed 2026-11-12, and the caller is calling about 'The statement of benefit charges the clinic received for the third quarter of 2026'; the docstring fixes the format 'YYYY-Qn'. Uniqueness: no other statement exists, and its window is open (day 12 of 30).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.protest_ground: wrong_wages. Basis: the docstring: 'wrong_wages means the base-period wages charged to this employer are wrong'; the caller says the clinic's 2025 wages for the claimant were reported twice and the amended 2025 reports cut each quarter by 3,150.00. Uniqueness: not_base_period_employer is excluded because the clinic did employ and pay her (separating employer on the claim, wages remain on the amended reports); the separation grounds, continuing_part_time and refused_suitable_work concern the separation, which is not disputed; agency_error and overpayment_recovered concern payments, not the wages; none is no ground.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.protested_amount: 274.88 = protested principal 272.16 + protest interest 2.72. Starting amount (statement_starting_amount: reimbursing class and a 2026-Q3 bill exist) = 3,908.10 billed; credits taken out (credits_taken_out: recovered-overpayment credits are among the credits posted in a quarter other than the statement's quarter) = every credit posted outside 2026-Q3 = 3,945.90 - 378.00 = 3,567.90 (the 378.00 cancelled-payment credit of 2026-09-30 was posted in the statement's own quarter, is already netted in the 3,908.10 bill, and stays; the rule names the quarter test, so there is no 'since' reading); disputed principal = 340.20; protest documentation share = 1.00 (four amended reports filed 2026-11-18 within twelve months; the 2025-08-14 amendment is outside); answer share = 0.80 (no separation response on record); protested principal = RND(340.20 x 1.00 x 0.80) = 272.16; interest months = 1 (bill due 2026-11-13, paid 2026-11-19: 0 whole months + 1); monthly protest interest (protest_interest_basis: interest assessed for 2026-Q3) = latest assessed month 39.08 x 272.16 / 3,908.10 = 2.72153; protest interest = RND(2.72153 x 1) = 2.72.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.relief_credit_amount: 272.16 = RND(MN(MX(0, relief reach - credits deducted) x answer abatement, charge still standing 340.20)). Relief reach (relief_reach: recorded ground wrong_wages is a wage-record ground) = every charge posted on the claim 4,286.10 x wage-record relief share 1.00 (four amended reports within twelve months); credits deducted (credits_deducted: a recovered-overpayment credit stands) = every credit posted 3,945.90; standing 340.20; answer abatement 0.80 (no separation response on record); 340.20 x 0.80 = 272.16.

protest_documentation_share (parameter): amended 2025-Q1..Q4 reports filed 2026-11-18 = 4 within twelve months (the 2024-Q4 amendment of 2025-08-14 is 15 months back) -> 1.00; baseline zero would give 0.00.

interest_months (method): bill due 2026-11-13, payment 2026-11-19 -> paid late -> MONTHS = 0 whole months + 1 = 1; baseline (no interest month) would give 272.16.

edges.condition: The charge position is in protest_pending status with a protest_date and a protest_ground other than none, and a charge protest submission for the protested statement quarter is on record for it.
edges.policy_source: The relief credit of a protest decision is fixed only after the position carries a pending written protest of the statement, with the protest ground and the protest date recorded on it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the position carries no written protest: its status is chargeable, its protest ground is none and its protest date is empty, and no charge protest submission exists for it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's protest write (step 11) sets status protest_pending, protest_date 2026-11-24 and protest_ground wrong_wages and records a charge_protest submission for 2026-Q3; the relief reach then reads the wage-record ground and the relief credit moves from 0.00 to 272.16.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the protest must land before the decision because the decision's relief reach reads the protest ground and quarter the protest records; reversing them gives a relief credit of 0.00 on a position with no protest.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the protest write leaves protest_ground none, so relief_reach takes the no-charge tier and relief_credit_amount recomputes to 0.00 instead of 272.16 (check_compute value_input run); the terminal state also lacks the charge_protest submission and the position never passes through protest_pending.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names a protest or any written submission as something to do: the caller only asks for the charges to be removed and leaves the decision to the agent; the only mention is the passive branch 'If the agent explains that the clinic itself has to put something in writing on record before the charges can be decided, you agree', which fires only after the agent explains it, and it names no ground, quarter or amount.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e performs ctx.create on charge_ledger and ctx.update on charge_positions with no check of status, protest ground or any earlier submission; called on the opening world it would still relieve the position and post the credit it is given. file_charge_protest_73ec7ae2 likewise writes without checking the window or status.
